text:
Trevor van Riemsdyk came off injured reserve on Nov 15 and picked up an assist in his first game back, against St. Louis on Nov 19, per CBS Sports. He had missed more than a month after five games to open the season.

He's 35, a Stanley Cup winner as a Chicago rookie in 2015, and on his fourth NHL team after a long run in Washington. Pittsburgh has put him straight back into 19 minutes a night.

The sample is seven games, so there's not much to say about this season's numbers. The Penguins are slightly behind in expected goals with him on at five on five. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season, 85th percentile among defensemen, with most of his value on the penalty kill. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 31% of his shots coming off the rush, high for a defenseman, and flagged his exits as a weak spot.

The Penguins have lost both games since his return. What to watch: whether a veteran's steadiness helps a blue line that has struggled to keep the puck out.
